title: Cohomology of a finite coproduct is the product of component cohomologies
statement: Let $C=\coprod_{i\in I}C_i$ be a finite coproduct of schemes [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] with each inclusion $C_i\hookrightarrow C$ open and closed. For an abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $C_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], the canonical restriction maps identify $H^q(C,F)$ with the finite product $\prod_{i\in I}H^q(C_i,F|_{C_i})$ for every $q\ge 0$, where $F|_{C_i}=\iota_i^{-1}F$ is the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] along the inclusion $\iota_i:C_i\hookrightarrow C$.

source.place: first paragraph of the proof of Lemma 0A5B (etale-cohomology-lemma-constant-smooth-statements), finite-product assembly over open-and-closed components

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], the coprojections \iota_i identify the summands C_i with pairwise disjoint open-and-closed subschemes covering C. Thus every etale object over C restricts to etale objects over the C_i, and the restriction maps are componentwise.

source.place: first paragraph of the proof of Lemma 0A5B (etale-cohomology-lemma-constant-smooth-statements), finite disjoint-union decomposition

proof.text: The sheaf condition on the finite family of open-and-closed inclusions says that a sheaf F on C is uniquely determined by the family of restrictions \iota_i^{-1}F, and every family of component sheaves glues uniquely because intersections between distinct summands are empty. Hence restriction is an equivalence with the finite product of the component sheaf categories. On the final object C, this equivalence identifies F(C) with the finite product of the component sections (\iota_i^{-1}F)(C_i). The inverse-image notation is the functor of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

source.place: first paragraph of the proof of Lemma 0A5B (etale-cohomology-lemma-constant-smooth-statements), finite-product assembly

proof.text: For every scheme T the category Ab(T_{Et}) has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], and the global-sections functor \Gamma(T_{Et},-) [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor] is additive and left exact, being a right adjoint (of the constant-sheaf functor). Etale cohomology H^q(T_{Et},F) is defined [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] as \mathcal H^q(\Gamma(T,I^\bullet)) for a K-injective resolution F\to I^\bullet; an injective resolution of F is a bounded below complex of injectives, hence K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so H^q(T_{Et},F)=R^q\Gamma(T_{Et},-)(F) in the sense of [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. The equivalence of Step 2 carries injective objects and injective resolutions in Ab(C_{Et}) to those of \prod_i Ab((C_i)_{Et}) and carries \Gamma(C_{Et},-) to the product functor of the \Gamma((C_i)_{Et},-) [lem-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-clopen-product]; so R^q\Gamma(C_{Et},-)(F) is R^q of the product functor at (\iota_i^{-1}F)_i. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-derived-finite-product] (each Ab((C_i)_{Et}) has enough injectives and each \Gamma((C_i)_{Et},-) is additive left exact, as above) gives, naturally for every q\ge0, H^q(C,F)\cong\prod_{i\in I}H^q(C_i,\iota_i^{-1}F). These isomorphisms are induced by restriction, so they are the canonical restriction maps in the statement; the product is finite.
